Module 01 • Nigerian CNG proposition

From abundant molecules to bankable mobility

A CNG market only works when supply, compression, logistics, dispensing and vehicle demand reinforce each other.

2ProcessingQuality and fuel specification
3CompressionHigh-pressure equipment

The 2023–2026 timeline
2023

Petrol subsidy reform changes fleet economics.

2024

Customs publicises certain gas-utilisation fiscal incentives.

MAR 2026

Pi-CNG mandate formally includes electric vehicles.

MAY 2026

Four MDGIF-supported CNG projects commissioned.

SEP–OCT

National affordable transit focus and renewed safety scrutiny.

Distinguish the fuels

CNG

Compressed, methane-rich natural gas. Automotive storage and refuelling require pressure-rated systems.

LPG

Liquefied petroleum gas, largely propane and butane. Not interchangeable with CNG equipment.

LNG

Liquefied methane stored at cryogenic temperature. Different economics, plant and logistics.

Investor test: No network scale-up assumption should survive without supplier deliverability, independent station status checks, conversion availability and demand verification.

Safety and tax

Module 03 • The 2026 Nigerian fiscal architecture

Tax classification is a transaction-level decision

2024 policy announcements and 2026 statutory requirements must not be treated as identical legal authorities. Review each supply's date, category and governing instruments.

18 December 2024 • Customs statement

Publicised zero import duties for specified Nigerian gas-utilisation machinery and zero-rated VAT treatment for enumerated CNG supplies, kits and services.

From 1 January 2026 • Nigeria Tax Act 2025

The Eleventh Schedule addresses possible suspension/delay of VAT charging on CNG and permits ministerial classification of relevant equipment and services as exempt or zero-rated, subject to the applicable Gazette orders.

Four VAT treatments: different legal and financial outcomes
Taxable
VAT charged as prescribed; input treatment depends on applicable law.
Zero-rated
Qualifying supplies at 0%; input VAT recovery differs from exemption and is governed by statute.
Exempt
No output VAT charged; input VAT may become a cost depending on the statute.
Suspended / delayed
Charging/collection timing governed by operative legislation and ministerial instrument; not automatically the same as exempt or zero-rated.
Client due diligence matrix
TransactionTax and legal checkpointsTypical audit / evidence request
Import CNG kit or compressorTariff code; import duty; effective incentives; customs valuation; import VATBill of entry, classification letter, procurement invoice, eligibility order
Sell transport CNGVAT application to CNG supply; invoicing; CIT; local leviesInvoices, readings, receipts, tax treatment memo
Convert fleet vehiclesConversion/installation VAT classification; asset recognition; WHTSON-approved kits, NADDC-accredited service, contract and invoice
Related-party gas tradeTransfer pricing, benchmarking, cost allocation, WHT where applicableIntercompany contracts, FAR, meter and logistics records
Finance CNG assetsTax deductibility, tax depreciation/allowances, withholding, FX, lease characterisationFinancing schedules, leases, debt covenants, contemporaneous tax advice
Professional caveat: This is a training framework, not a ruling that all CNG transactions enjoy zero VAT or zero customs duty in November 2026. Ascertain the actual operative Ministerial/Gazette orders, legal commencement, circulars and tariff treatment for the transaction.
Interactive prompt: Ask participants how input tax treatment changes when a transaction is exempt rather than zero-rated, and why incentives should be tested against the date of the supply.
Module 04 • Controls, standards and disclosures

Safety, accounting and climate claims all affect value

Good economics cannot compensate for uncertified conversion kits, unsupported regulatory status, weak meter reconciliation or misleading sustainability disclosures.

Safety event • 13 September 2026

Pi-CNG & EV reported an Abuja refuelling cylinder incident involving an unauthorised cylinder. Its 14 September statement called for SON-certified automotive CNG equipment, NADDC-accredited conversion and NMDPRA-licensed stations.

ISO 16923:2026

International guidance for the design, construction, operation, maintenance and inspection of CNG refuelling stations. Determine local enforceability separately.

IFRS S1 / S2 in Nigeria

The FRC updated its sustainability reporting roadmap in 2026. An SEC circular dated 23 September 2026 sought adoption implementation plans from relevant public companies and significant market operators by 15 October 2026.

Accounting and assurance standards map
StandardCommon CNG-related issuePotential challenge to management
IAS 16Compressors, dispensers, conversion kits, asset components and useful livesIs expenditure capital or expense? What replacement cycles are justified?
IFRS 16Station, fleet and land lease agreementsAre there embedded leases, variable payments or modifications?
IFRS 9Loans to fleet operators and credit salesDo stress scenarios change credit risk and ECL?
IAS 36Stranded infrastructure, poor volume, adverse tariffsDoes recoverable amount support station or conversion-kit carrying values?
IAS 37HSE incident provision and contingent liabilitiesIs a present obligation measurable? Is disclosure required?
IFRS S1/S2Climate assumptions, methane measurement, governance and transition claimsAre reporting boundaries, controls and targets traceable to credible evidence?

CNG is not “zero carbon”. Any claimed lifecycle advantage depends on supply-chain methane, compression energy and measured vehicle performance.
Module 05 • Tailored for EY professionals

EY client impact: financial, fiscal, operational and climate

The practical question is where to create measurable client value while respecting all applicable audit and non-audit independence restrictions.

Assurance & financial reporting

  • Reconcile gas stock, compressor output and CNG sales to revenue.
  • Review fleet conversion accounting, depreciation, leases, impairment and ECL.
  • Assure sustainability information against controlled source records.

Tax & transfer pricing

  • Build 2026 VAT and Customs classification memos by transaction.
  • Validate capital allowances, contracts, payments and withholding.
  • Benchmark related-party gas, logistics, compression and branding charges.

Strategy & transactions

  • Develop bankable DCF with tariff, demand and uptime sensitivity.
  • Test security package, anchor demand and downside lender cover.
  • Perform licences, HSE, vendor and capex due diligence.

Digital controls & sustainability

  • Integrate dispenser telemetry, inventory, billing and ERP.
  • Detect revenue leakage, meter overrides and suspicious transactions.
  • Implement credible methane metrics, board reporting and IFRS S2 controls.
EY client pipeline: a 90-day intervention
01–30

Diagnose

Value chain mapping, regulatory status, tax logic, investment assumptions, HSE and controls baseline.

31–60

Underwrite

Demand, fleet/station economics, financing alternatives and implementation-ready controls.

61–90

Assure and decide

Investment gate, pilot KPIs, governance, climate evidence and execution workstreams.

Reference library • verified context at 1 November 2026

Transparent sources and model limitations

Prefer statutes, regulator releases, primary programme records and professional standards. Download and review current legal instruments before relying upon any treatment.

Important modelling and legal caveats

Prices and conversions are hypothetical

₦1,400/L petrol, ₦600/scm CNG, vehicle efficiency and conversion capex are teaching assumptions, not verified Nigerian pump prices. Standard cubic metres and litres are not directly equivalent. Measure vehicle-specific km/unit.

NPV and IRR are simplified

The DCF excludes capital allowance timing, gas-supply prepayments, terminal value, tax-loss utilisation, financing fees, working-capital volatility and project-specific inflation. The financing coverage metric is a proxy, not an audited lender DSCR.

Legal status is date-specific

Public 2024 customs announcements cannot determine every 2026 transaction. Obtain legal advice on the Nigeria Tax Act, operative Gazette instruments, import tariff classification and current local implementation.

Publicly reported KPIs require verification

Pi-CNG & EV web pages display some varying station totals. In this presentation, 105 is a dated programme count of 15 October 2026; it is not an independently audited current capacity measure.
